title: Cheltenham Dispatch — Ink-Deep Feature Opener
description: A faithful recreation of the NYT Magazine long-form opener: a bleed photograph anchors the right gutter while a red small-caps kicker, two-line serif headline, byline strip, and drop-capped opening column command the left. What separates it from generic editorial templates is the locked typographic hierarchy — nothing floats, nothing centers.
philosophy: This template exists for the slide that must feel like it was torn from a serious magazine, not assembled in a design tool. It values the authority of editorial restraint: one accent color, one typeface family, one job per element. It refuses decorative flourish, icon sets, and anything that competes with the headline. The room it is built for is quiet, the audience is reading, and the speaker is a writer first.
goodFor: Opening slides for essay-style keynote or lecture presentations
Media, journalism, and publishing industry pitch decks
Long-form thought-leadership on AI, culture, or policy with gravitas
Literary or academic conference feature slides anchored by a single argument
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring scannable data
Startup pitch decks that need kinetic visual energy and high color contrast
Workshop decks built around rapid bullet-point summaries
Social-media ad assets where headline legibility at thumbnail size is critical
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should evoke a serious magazine's opening spread — weighty, still, and self-assured. The left column commands via typographic authority alone: a small-caps kicker labels the section, a two-line headline lands with editorial finality, and a byline strip closes the text block without ornamentation. The right half is surrendered fully to a bleed-edge atmospheric photograph that amplifies the headline's thesis rather than illustrates it. Nothing floats, nothing centers — this composition is built on gravity, not gesture.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid splits the slide into two asymmetric halves — the left six columns carry all text elements flush-left with an 8% outer margin; the right six columns are consumed entirely by a full-bleed photograph extending to all four slide edges. Kicker label anchors the top of the text column, followed immediately by a thin horizontal rule, then the two-line headline, then a byline strip sitting near the lower third. No element crosses the center axis; typographic hierarchy is enforced by size contrast and the single rule line alone, with no decorative separators or background fields.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the interior spread of a considered long-form magazine piece — quiet, paper-weighted, built for a reader who is leaning in rather than scanning. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric and column-anchored: the left mass of text carries authority while the right rail offers a contrasting secondary note (a sidebar attribution, a short pull quote, or a captioned secondary image) without competing. The single accent color appears only as punctuation — a kicker label, a rule line — never as decoration. Avoid any element that floats, centers, or gestures toward infographic logic; every object must belong to a column and serve one explicit editorial function.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a locked left-rail body zone occupying cols 1–7 and a right sidebar zone in cols 9–12 separated by a single hairline rule. Primary content block — either a drop-capped opening paragraph, a pull quote with flanking rule lines above and below, or a two-item feature list with bold label + body text pairs — sits flush left in the body zone with no center alignment anywhere. A small-caps section kicker anchors the top of col 1, a thin horizontal rule runs beneath it at roughly 12% from the top, and the folio (page number + deck title slug) sits bottom-right outside the grid. No header band; hierarchy is enforced by size contrast and rule lines alone.
